_**Tijuana Moods**_ is an album by Charles Mingus, recorded in 1957 but not released until June 1962.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-CashBox-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-Billboard-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-3) This delay was due to a legal dispute with RCA.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-4) The album was reissued in 1986 on CD as _New Tijuana Moods_ with four additional alternate takes and as a double LP with five alternate takes. Two-CD expanded versions with further alternate takes were issued by RCA in 2000 and by Columbia in 2010.
In his notes to the 1986 reissue, Ed Michel said that "[h]ardly anything was recorded as a complete take" and so both the originally issued takes and the alternate versions had been assembled by editing additional sections into base takes.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-5)

The name "Charlie Mingus" appears on the cover of the original album. Mingus hated all nicknames derived from Charles. ("Don't call me Charlie; that's not a man's name, that's a name for a horse."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana_Moods#cite_note-6))

# Recorded on July 18 and August 6, 1957 in NYC... Charles Mingus - Tijuana Moods
Charles Mingus - Tijuana Moods
Recorded on July 18 and August 6, 1957 in NYC, but not released until June 1962.
Clarence Shaw - trumpet; Jimmy Knepper - trombone; Curtis Porter - tenor, alto sax; Bill Triglia - piano; Charles Mingus - bass; Dannie Richmond - drums; Frankie Dunlop - tambourine, castanets; Ysabel Morel - vocal, handclaps; Lonne Elder - narrator;
All compositions by Charles Mingus except where noted.
"Dizzy Moods"
"Ysabel's Table Dance"
"Tijuana Gift Shop"
"Los Mariachis (The Street Musicians)"
"Flamingo" (Ted Grouya)
"A Colloquial Dream (Scenes in the City)"
The name "Charlie Mingus" appears on the cover of the original album. Mingus hated all nicknames derived from Charles.

# Josef Newgarden wins IndyCar Phoenix race with late-race pass
*   Story by       
*   Josef Newgarden wins IndyCar Phoenix race with late-race pass
Nick Gray, Nashville Tennessean·AZCentral | The Arizona Republic
Sun, Mar 8, 2026·
1 min read
Josef Newgarden is back in victory lane in the NTT IndyCar Series.
Newgarden moved through the top 10 on a short final run, taking the lead from Kyle Kirkwood with seven laps to go to win the Good Ranchers 250 on March 7 at Phoenix Raceway.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
The Hendersonville native now leads in the IndyCar points standings through two races.
Team Penske's top driver had a tire advantage on the final run, which began with 31 laps to go. He quickly moved into the top five, then made the move on Christian Rasmussen (who got into the wall) with about 10 laps to go for second before reaching Kirkwood for the top spot.
The 2025 season was arguably Newgarden's worst in more than a decade. While he finished the year with a win at Nashville, it was his only victory of the year filled with several DNFs and potential good finishes gone awry.
"Momentum is a big deal," Newgarden said to FOX during his victory lane interview. "I don't know. It's very difficult to understand how things work. Sometimes, things go against us. Sometimes they go for us."
